# Case sensitivity flag in Parser is inverted

When creating a Parser object with the case_sensitive parameter, the behavior is opposite of what's expected.

## Description

The case_sensitive flag in the Parser class is working backwards. When setting case_sensitive=True, the parser actually ignores case, and when setting case_sensitive=False (the default), the parser is case sensitive.

## Reproduction

```python
import parse

# Default behavior (case_sensitive=False) is actually case sensitive
result = parse.parse('SPAM {} SPAM', 'spam spam spam')
print(result)  # None - doesn't match because case is different

# Setting case_sensitive=True makes it ignore case
result = parse.parse('SPAM {} SPAM', 'spam spam spam', case_sensitive=True)
print(result)  # Matches and returns ['spam']

# Same issue with findall
results = parse.findall('x({})x', 'X(hi)X')
print(list(results))  # [] - doesn't match because case is different

results = parse.findall('x({})x', 'X(hi)X', case_sensitive=True)
print(list(results))  # Matches and returns results with 'hi'
```

This is confusing because the parameter name suggests the opposite behavior. When I set case_sensitive=True, I expect the parser to be sensitive to case differences, but it's actually ignoring case.
</pr_description>
